title: spice-scented roast chicken and vegetables
ingredients: Chicken, 1 (2¾–3 lb), cut into 8 pieces; olive oil, 4 tbsp; low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp; mustard seeds, 1 tbsp; cumin seeds, 1 tbsp; onion, 1, finely chopped; salt and pepper; fingerling or small red potatoes, 1–1¼ lb, halved; asparagus, 2 bunches (about 1 lb), trimmed.
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss chicken with 2 tbsp oil, soy sauce, ground mustard and cumin seeds, onion, salt, and pepper; arrange skin-side up on half a baking sheet.

Toss potatoes with 1 tbsp oil, reserved spices, salt, and pepper; arrange cut-side down beside chicken. Roast about 40 minutes. Toss asparagus with remaining oil, salt, and pepper; roast on a lower rack until tender-crisp, about 10 minutes. Transfer everything to a platter and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Chicken, potatoes, and asparagus cook together as a complete meal.

title: roasted salmon with thyme vinaigrette
ingredients: Dijon mustard, ½ tbsp; Champagne or white wine vinegar, 2 tsp; extra-virgin olive oil, 2½ tbsp, plus more; shallot, 1 tbsp minced; fresh thyme, 2 tsp minced; salt and pepper; salmon fillet, about ¾ lb; mixed baby lettuces, 3 cups.
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Whisk mustard and vinegar, then gradually whisk in 2½ tbsp oil; stir in shallot and thyme and season. Oil a baking dish, add salmon skin-side down, spoon over half the vinaigrette, and marinate 15–20 minutes.
Roast salmon about 15 minutes, until almost cooked through. Toss lettuces with remaining vinaigrette; divide between plates, add salmon, and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Easily doubled; vinaigrette can be made a day ahead. Leftovers can be used for salmon salad.

title: Risotto with leeks and sugar snaps
ingredients: Low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 5½ cups; sugar snap peas, 1 lb, trimmed; olive oil, 1 tbsp; pancetta, 3 oz, minced; leeks, 2, sliced; Arborio rice, 1½ cups; dry white wine, ½ cup; Parmesan, 1 cup grated; fresh tarragon, 1 tbsp minced; salt and pepper.
instructions: Bring broth to a boil, cook snap peas until tender-crisp, about 2 minutes, remove them, and keep broth hot. Sauté pancetta in oil, add leeks and cook until tender, then stir in rice until opaque. Add wine and stir until absorbed.

Add hot broth about ¾ cup at a time, stirring frequently and allowing each addition to absorb, until rice is creamy and just tender, about 20 minutes. Stir in peas, Parmesan, tarragon, and pepper; adjust seasoning and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers can be made into risotto cakes with egg yolk and panko.

title: mustard-peppercorn steak and arugula salad
ingredients: Peppercorns, 2 tsp; mustard seeds, 1 tsp; fresh rosemary, 1 tbsp minced; salt, 2 tsp; top sirloin steak, 1¼ lb; olive oil; balsamic vinegar, ½ cup; shallots, ¼ cup minced; brown sugar, 1 tsp; arugula, 6 cups; red onion, ¼, sliced; radishes, ½ bunch, sliced; lemon, ½.
instructions: Coarsely grind peppercorns and mustard seeds; mix with rosemary and salt. Pat steak dry and press seasoning onto both sides. Sear in an oiled heavy pan over high heat, about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare; rest.

Boil vinegar, shallots, and sugar in the pan until reduced to a glaze. Divide arugula among plates; top with onion and radishes and squeeze lemon over. Slice steak thinly, arrange on salad, drizzle with glaze, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Slice meat thinly; leftover steak is good in sandwiches.

title: linguine, shrimp, and endive with bread crumbs
ingredients: Whole-grain or sourdough bread, 2 slices; olive oil, 4 tbsp; large shallot, 1 minced; fresh thyme, 1 tbsp plus 2 tsp minced; salt and pepper; dried linguine, ¾–1 lb; large onion, 1 chopped; red pepper flakes, ½ tsp; fresh rosemary, 2 tsp minced; large shrimp, 1 lb peeled and deveined; endive, 4 heads, sliced; lemon juice, 3 tbsp; flat-leaf parsley, chopped.
instructions: Grind bread to crumbs. Sauté shallot in 2 tbsp oil, add 1 tbsp thyme and 1½ cups crumbs, and cook until crisp; season and set aside. Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente.

Sauté onion, pepper flakes, and rosemary in remaining oil. Add shrimp, season, and cook briefly; turn, add endive and remaining thyme, and sauté until shrimp are cooked and endive softens. Add lemon juice and reduce. Toss drained pasta with shrimp mixture and some reserved pasta water. Top with crumbs and parsley.
notes: Makes 4 servings.

title: Chicken breasts with lentil-raisin-mint salad
ingredients: Brown lentils, 1 cup; small red onion, 1, halved; bay leaf, 1; salt; red wine vinegar, 2 tbsp plus 1 tsp; celery ribs, 2 chopped; radishes, 1 bunch sliced; fresh mint, 7 tbsp minced; extra-virgin olive oil, ½ cup plus 2 tbsp; boneless skinless chicken breast halves, 4; flour for dredging.
instructions: Simmer lentils with half the onion and bay leaf until just tender, about 30 minutes. Stir in salt and 1 tsp vinegar, drain, discard cooked onion and bay leaf. Mix lentils with chopped remaining onion, celery, radishes, and 3 tbsp mint.

Whisk remaining vinegar with ½ cup oil and remaining mint; season. Reserve 3 tbsp dressing, then mix enough remaining dressing into lentil salad. Flatten chicken slightly, season, dredge in flour, and sauté in oil until cooked through, 4–5 minutes per side. Slice and serve with salad and reserved dressing.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Salad can be made a day ahead; leftover chicken is good in sandwiches.

title: beef medallions with spring mashed potatoes
ingredients: Yukon gold potatoes, 1½ lb, peeled and cubed; salt and pepper; olive oil, 3 tbsp; small savoy cabbage, ½ head, sliced; unsalted butter, 1–2 tbsp; beef tri-tip roast, 1¼ lb; shallots, 2 sliced; flour, 1 tbsp; low-sodium beef broth, 2 cups; dry vermouth, 2 tbsp; Dijon mustard, 2 tsp; fresh thyme, 1½ tbsp minced, plus garnish.
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 10 minutes. Sauté cabbage in 1 tbsp oil until nearly tender. Reserve 1 cup potato water, drain and coarsely mash potatoes with butter, cabbage, pepper, and enough cooking water; keep warm.

Slice beef across the grain into thin strips. Sear in batches in 1 tbsp oil, about 30 seconds per side; season and set aside. Sauté shallots in remaining oil until golden. Stir in flour, then broth and vermouth; simmer until slightly thickened. Stir in mustard and thyme, optionally finish with butter. Serve beef and potatoes with sauce and thyme.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Freeze meat briefly for easier slicing; leftovers make sandwiches.

title: pizza with pancetta, asparagus, and goat cheese
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp; pancetta, 2 oz minced; red pepper flakes, ¼ tsp; slender asparagus, 1 bunch; pizza dough, 1 lb; cornmeal; whole-milk mozzarella, 6 oz shredded; green onions, 4 sliced; fresh goat cheese, ¼ lb crumbled; Parmesan; salt and pepper.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°F. Sauté pancetta and pepper flakes in 1 tbsp oil until browned. Cut asparagus into pieces and toss with remaining oil. Roll dough into an 11–12-inch round and place on a cornmeal-dusted sheet. Brush with pancetta oil; add pancetta, mozzarella, green onions, goat cheese, and asparagus. Season and grate Parmesan over.
Bake about 20 minutes, until asparagus is tender and crust browned. Rest 5 minutes, cut, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Prepared fresh pizza dough is suggested; tips offer topping variations.

title: Sautéed tilapia with green onion–ginger raita
ingredients: Plain yogurt, ⅔ cup; olive oil, 3 tbsp; green onions, 4 minced; fresh ginger, 2 tsp minced; fresh cilantro, 2 tbsp minced, plus leaves; salt and pepper; tilapia fillets, 4; Madras curry powder, 2 tsp.
instructions: Sauté green onions and ginger in 2 tbsp oil until fragrant; stir into yogurt with cilantro and season to make raita. Season fish with curry powder, salt, and pepper. Heat remaining oil and sauté fish 2–3 minutes per side, until just cooked. Serve with raita.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Raita can be prepared a day ahead; trout, Arctic char, or salmon may replace tilapia.

title: mushroom and manchego quesadillas
ingredients: Serrano chiles, 1½; cherry or pear tomatoes, ⅔ cup quartered; cilantro, 2 tbsp minced; green onion, 1 sliced; salt and pepper; olive oil, 2 tbsp; shallots, 2 minced; cremini mushrooms, 10 oz sliced; small corn tortillas, 6; Manchego, 5 oz shredded.
instructions: Seed and chop one chile and mince the remaining half. Mix tomatoes, cilantro, green onion, and minced chile for salsa; season. Sauté shallots in oil, add mushrooms and chopped chile, season, and cook until juices evaporate.
Warm tortillas on a griddle. Add cheese and mushrooms to half of each, fold, and cook until golden and crisp, about 3 minutes per side. Serve with salsa.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Recipe can be doubled; keep batches warm in a low oven.

title: asian-style chicken soup with baby bok choy
ingredients: Low-sodium chicken broth, 8 cups; green onions, 1 bunch; fresh ginger, 2-inch piece sliced; Asian fish sauce, 2 tbsp; sugar, 1 tbsp; star anise, 6 pods; cloves, 6; boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1–1¼ lb; Thai chiles, 3 (or serrano, 1); bean sprouts, basil, cilantro, lime wedges, and optional hoisin to serve; baby bok choy, 4; dried rice-stick noodles, 6–7 oz; salt and pepper.
instructions: Combine broth and 2 cups water with halved green onions, ginger, fish sauce, sugar, star anise, and cloves. Bring to a boil; add chicken, return to boil, then simmer until cooked, 10–15 minutes. Remove chicken and simmer broth 15–30 minutes longer.

Set out sliced green onions, chiles, sprouts, herbs, lime, and optional hoisin. Slice bok choy and chicken. Soak noodles 3 minutes in very hot water. Strain aromatics from broth, season, add bok choy and bring to a boil; drain noodles and cook in broth about 2 minutes. Divide noodles, bok choy, and chicken among bowls; ladle broth over and serve with condiments.
notes: Makes 4 servings.

title: goat cheese soufflé with fresh herbs
ingredients: Butter for dish; Parmesan or dried bread crumbs; extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup; shallots, 2 minced; flour, 5 tbsp; whole milk, 1¼ cups; dry white wine, ¼ cup; large eggs, 6; egg whites, 2; salt, 1 tsp; lemon thyme or thyme, 1 tsp; tarragon, 2½ tsp; soft goat cheese, 1½ cups crumbled; pepper.
instructions: Heat oven to 400°F. Butter a 10-cup soufflé dish and coat with Parmesan. Sauté shallots in oil; stir in flour, then gradually whisk in milk and wine. Cook until smooth and thick. Separate eggs; whisk some hot mixture into yolks, return to pan, and mix in salt, herbs, cheese, and pepper.

Beat whites to stiff peaks. Fold a quarter into cheese mixture, then fold in remaining whites. Transfer to dish, lower oven to 375°F, and bake about 35 minutes, until puffed, golden, and gently set. Serve immediately.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Can be assembled an hour ahead; tips explain separating eggs.

title: seared beef salad with thai flavors
ingredients: Top sirloin, 1 lb; lemongrass, 2 tbsp minced; fish sauce, 2 tbsp; low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp; sugar, 1½ tsp; shallots, 2 minced; pepper; peanut oil, 4 tbsp; lime juice, 3 tbsp; serrano chiles, 1½–2 minced; salt; red leaf lettuce, 1 head; bean sprouts, ¾ lb; Persian cucumbers, 4; basil, 1 cup; mint, ⅓ cup; red onion, ½ sliced.
instructions: Freeze beef 30 minutes, slice thinly across the grain. Mix lemongrass, 1 tbsp fish sauce, soy, half the sugar and shallots, and pepper. Coat beef and marinate 15–30 minutes.

Whisk 3 tbsp oil with lime juice, chiles, remaining fish sauce, sugar, and shallots; season. Toss lettuce, sprouts, cucumbers, basil, mint, and onion with dressing. Sear beef in batches in remaining oil, about 20 seconds per side. Arrange over salad and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Dressing can be prepared ahead; lemon zest can replace lemongrass.

title: spaghetti carbonara with black kale
ingredients: Pancetta, 3 oz chopped; shallot, 1 minced; dry white wine, ¼ cup; dried spaghetti, 6–8 oz; black kale, 1 bunch chopped; eggs, 2; Parmesan, ½ cup grated; Romano, ¼ cup grated; black pepper.
instructions: Sauté pancetta until browning; add shallot, then wine, and reduce by half. Remove from heat. Cook spaghetti 5 minutes in salted water; add kale and cook until pasta is al dente.

Beat eggs with cheeses and pepper. Reserve ½ cup pasta water, then drain. Reheat pancetta briefly, remove from heat, and toss with pasta and kale. Gradually whisk ¼ cup pasta water into egg mixture, then stir into pasta until creamy; use very low heat briefly only if needed. Add more water for silky texture and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Remove pan from heat before adding eggs to prevent curdling.

title: Roast chicken with young potatoes and carrots
ingredients: Chicken, 1 (OCR weight unclear); fresh tarragon, 4 sprigs plus 4 tsp minced; fresh thyme, 4 sprigs plus 4 tsp minced; salt and pepper; young potatoes, 2 lb halved; carrots, 2 lb in pieces; olive oil, 2 tbsp; dry white wine, ½ cup.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°F and grease a heavy rimmed baking sheet. Remove giblets, dry chicken, loosen breast skin, and tuck in tarragon and thyme sprigs. Season with minced herbs, salt, and pepper; put remaining sprigs in cavity. Roast 30 minutes.

Toss potatoes and carrots with oil, 2 tsp each minced herb, salt, and pepper. Remove chicken, spoon off most fat, arrange vegetables around it, and roast about 40 minutes more, until thigh registers 165°F. Transfer vegetables and chicken to a platter. Degrease pan juices; deglaze baking sheet with wine, boil to reduce, add chicken juices and remaining herbs, season, carve, and serve with sauce.
notes: Makes 4 servings.

title: Sautéed scallops and swiss chard
ingredients: Olive oil, 3 tbsp; chard, 1 small bunch, leaves chopped; salt and pepper; sea scallops, ¾ lb; flour for dredging; shallot, 1 minced; dry white wine, ¼ cup; low-sodium chicken broth, ½ cup; lemon juice, 1 tbsp; Dijon mustard, ½ tsp; tarragon, ½ tsp; optional butter, 1 tbsp; cooked brown rice; optional toasted pecans, 2 tbsp.
instructions: Sauté chard in 1 tbsp oil until softened, about 3 minutes; cover and keep warm. Season scallops, dredge in flour, and sauté in another 1 tbsp oil about 3 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.

Sauté shallot in remaining oil. Add wine and reduce almost completely. Add broth, lemon juice, mustard, and tarragon; simmer until slightly thickened. Off heat, stir in optional butter and season. Serve scallops and chard over rice with sauce, tarragon, and optional pecans.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Other hearty greens and thyme can replace chard and tarragon; recipe doubles easily.

title: chicken fajitas with savoy cabbage slaw
ingredients: Olive oil, 4 tbsp; chili powder, 2 tsp; dried oregano, 1 tsp; boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1¼ lb; red onions, 2; salt and pepper; 8–12 small tortillas; savoy cabbage, ½ head sliced; cilantro, ¼ cup chopped; lime juice, 2 tbsp; avocado, 1 sliced.
instructions: Mix 2 tbsp oil with chili powder and oregano. Slice chicken and onions; toss in mixture, season, and marinate while preparing other ingredients. Heat oven to 350°F and warm foil-wrapped tortillas about 15 minutes.

Toss cabbage and cilantro with remaining oil, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Warm an oiled griddle; cook chicken and onions, turning, until chicken is done and onions browned. Serve with tortillas, slaw, and avocado.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Slaw can be made a day ahead; steak or mahi mahi can replace chicken.

title: penne with ricotta cheese and greens
ingredients: Tuscan kale or hearty greens, 1 bunch; dried penne, 6–8 oz; extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp; fresh thyme, 2 tsp minced; shallot, 1 minced; lemon zest, 1 tsp; Parmesan, ½ cup grated; fresh whole-milk ricotta, ½ cup; salt and pepper.
instructions: Boil greens in salted water until just tender, 30 seconds to 6 minutes; remove and drain. Return water to boil and cook pasta until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water; drain pasta with greens.
Return pasta and greens to pot. Add oil, thyme, shallot, and zest; toss. Stir in cheeses, adding pasta water if needed to moisten. Season and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Easily doubled; cooking greens in pasta water saves a pot.

title: broccoli and comté frittata
ingredients: Broccoli, 1 lb; olive oil, 2 tbsp; country bread cubes, 1 cup; eggs, 10; chives, ⅓ cup minced; marjoram, 2 tbsp minced; salt and pepper; Comté or Gruyère, 1⅓ cups shredded; shallots, 2 sliced.
instructions: Steam broccoli until tender-crisp, about 4 minutes. Sauté bread cubes in 1 tbsp oil until golden. Beat eggs with herbs, salt, and pepper; mix in 1 cup cheese.

Sauté shallots in remaining oil until golden, add broccoli and heat through. Mix bread into eggs, pour into pan, stir gently, cover, and cook over medium-low until nearly set, about 12 minutes. Add remaining cheese and broil about 3 minutes, until puffed and browned. Loosen and slide onto platter.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers make sandwiches or room-temperature appetizers.

title: Lamb chops with mint salsa verde
ingredients: Mint leaves, ½ cup; flat-leaf parsley, ½ cup; shallot, 1; salt, ¼ tsp; red pepper flakes; extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup; lemon juice, 1½ tsp; pepper; lamb shoulder round-bone chops, 4.
instructions: Pulse mint, parsley, shallot, salt, and a pinch of pepper flakes in food processor to coarse paste. With machine running, add 3 tbsp oil and lemon juice; season with pepper.
Season lamb. Heat remaining oil in a heavy pan and cook chops about 3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Serve topped with salsa verde.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Extra salsa keeps in the refrigerator and can be thinned with olive oil.

title: black cod with lemon and thyme bread crumbs
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tsp plus more; black cod or Arctic char fillets, 4; lemon juice; salt and pepper; whole-grain or sourdough bread, 1 slice; shallot, 1 minced; lemon zest, 1 tbsp; fresh thyme, 1 tbsp minced.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°F and oil a rimmed baking sheet. Place fish skin-side down, brush with oil, add lemon juice, salt, and pepper; marinate while preparing topping. Grind bread to crumbs and mix ¾ cup with shallot, zest, thyme, 2 tsp oil, salt, and pepper.
Press crumb mixture onto fish just before baking. Bake about 10 minutes, until fish is springy and crumbs begin to brown. Serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Arctic char or tilapia may substitute.

title: stir-fried pork and sugar snaps with soba noodles
ingredients: Low-sodium soy sauce, 3½ tbsp; cornstarch, 1½ tsp; sesame oil, 1½ tsp plus 1 tbsp; pork, ½ lb, thinly sliced; pepper; rice wine vinegar, 2 tbsp; sugar, 1½ tsp; sugar snap peas, ½ lb; soba noodles, 6 oz; green onions, 1 bunch; peanut oil, 1 tbsp; ginger, 1 tbsp minced; red pepper flakes, ¼ tsp.
instructions: Mix 1½ tbsp soy sauce with cornstarch and 1½ tsp sesame oil; coat pork with mixture and pepper and marinate 15–30 minutes. Mix remaining soy and sesame oils with vinegar and sugar.

Boil peas until crisp-tender; remove. Cook noodles until tender, drain, and toss with half the sauce, peas, and most green onions. Stir-fry ginger and pepper flakes in peanut oil; add pork and cook through, 2–3 minutes. Add remaining sauce, thicken, toss with noodles, and garnish with reserved onions.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Doubles easily; leftovers are also good at room temperature.

title: citrus-herb turkey cutlets with baby broccoli
ingredients: Orange, 1; turkey breast cutlets, 1–1¼ lb; tarragon, 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp minced; salt and pepper; olive oil, 3 tbsp; flour for dredging; shallot, 1 minced; baby broccoli, ¾ lb; low-sodium chicken broth, 1 cup; optional butter, ½ tbsp.
instructions: Grate orange zest and measure ¼ cup juice. Season turkey with zest, 1 tbsp tarragon, salt, and pepper. Dredge half in flour and sauté in 1 tbsp oil until golden and cooked, 2–3 minutes per side; repeat with another tbsp oil.

Sauté shallot in remaining oil; add broccoli and broth, cover, and boil until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Transfer broccoli to platter. Reduce orange juice in pan until syrupy; add remaining tarragon and optional butter. Serve sauce over turkey with broccoli.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers can be mixed with rice and vinaigrette for a salad.

title: chicken sauté with sugar snaps and asparagus
ingredients: Flour for dredging; chicken tenders, 10 oz; salt and pepper; olive oil, 2 tbsp; thin asparagus, 1 bunch; sugar snap peas, ½ lb; low-sodium chicken broth, 1 cup; thyme, 1 tbsp minced; chives, 1 tbsp minced; lemon juice, 2 tbsp; optional thyme, chives, and lemon zest to garnish.
instructions: Cut tenders in half, season, and dredge in flour. Sauté in 1 tbsp oil until cooked, about 5 minutes; transfer to plate. Sauté asparagus in remaining oil, add peas and seasoning, then broth; cover and boil until vegetables nearly tender-crisp, about 3 minutes.
Return chicken to pan; add thyme, chives, and lemon juice. Simmer uncovered until sauce thickens and coats chicken, about 2 minutes. Serve with garnishes.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Flexible recipe: other herbs, peas, or zucchini may be used.

title: clams with white beans, fennel, and broccoli rabe
ingredients: Fennel bulb, 1, fronds reserved; fennel seeds, ½ tsp; olive oil, 1 tbsp plus more; red onion, ½ chopped; red pepper flakes, ¼–½ tsp; dry white wine, ½ cup; cannellini beans, 1 can; clam juice, 1 bottle; saffron; pepper; broccoli rabe or Chinese broccoli, ½ small bunch; Manila clams, 2 lb; optional salt.
instructions: Slice fennel and coarsely grind fennel seeds. Sauté fennel, seeds, onion, and pepper flakes in oil until softened, about 5 minutes. Add wine and boil off; add beans, clam juice, saffron, and pepper; simmer 5 minutes. Add broccoli rabe and cook until wilted.
Add clams and reserved bean liquid if needed. Cover and boil until clams open, about 5 minutes; season. Serve in deep bowls with olive oil and fennel fronds.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Double in a large Dutch oven.

title: grilled pizza with eggplant and tomatoes
ingredients: Extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup plus more; balsamic vinegar, ¼ cup; salt and pepper; Asian eggplants, 2 sliced; small red onion, 1 sliced; pizza dough, 1 lb; mozzarella, ½ lb shredded; cherry tomatoes, 1 cup halved; Romano, ½ cup grated; red pepper flakes, ½ tsp; basil, 3 tbsp slivered; marjoram, 2 tbsp minced.
instructions: Prepare grill for medium direct heat. Whisk oil and vinegar; season. Brush eggplant and onion with mixture and grill covered until tender and browned, about 5–6 minutes per side. Cut eggplant into pieces and separate onion rings.

Divide dough in half, roll into two 9-inch rounds, and grill oiled side down 3 minutes; turn and grill 2 minutes. Top grill-marked sides with mozzarella, vegetables, tomatoes, Romano, pepper flakes, and a little vinaigrette. Grill covered until cheese melts, 5–8 minutes. Finish with herbs and serve.
notes: Makes 2 pizzas; serves 4. Purchased fresh dough is suggested; toppings can be varied.

title: Zucchini, chile, and red onion frittata
ingredients: Poblano chile, 1; eggs, 8; salt and pepper; white Cheddar, ¼ lb shredded; olive oil, 1 tbsp; red onion, 1 sliced; zucchini, 2 sliced; cilantro, chopped.
instructions: Char chile over gas flame or under broiler; cool, peel, seed, and chop. Beat eggs with salt and pepper and stir in ¾ cup cheese.

Sauté onion in oil until nearly tender; add zucchini, season, and cook until tender. Stir in chile, pour in eggs, and cook covered over medium-low until nearly set, about 10 minutes. Add remaining cheese and broil about 3 minutes until puffed and browned. Loosen, slide onto platter, sprinkle with cilantro, and cut into wedges.
notes: Makes 4 servings. For faster preparation, sauté chile with onion instead of charring.

title: grilled tuna with basil-walnut sauce
ingredients: Albacore tuna steaks, 2, 1 inch thick; salt and pepper; lemon zest, 1; extra-virgin olive oil, 1½ tbsp plus more; basil leaves, ¼ cup; walnut pieces, 1 tbsp.
instructions: Season tuna with salt, pepper, and lemon zest; brush with oil and marinate briefly. Process basil, walnuts, ⅛ tsp salt, and pepper until finely ground; with processor running, add olive oil to make sauce.
Grill tuna over high heat to desired doneness and serve with basil-walnut sauce.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Sauce can be thinned with oil and used with fish, chicken, or potatoes.

title: corn and cheddar fritters with sautéed tomatoes
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp plus more; red onion, ½ finely chopped; red bell pepper, ½ chopped; kernels from 1 large ear corn; salt and pepper; cornmeal, ⅔ cup; flour, 3 tbsp; sugar, 1 tsp; cayenne, ¼ tsp plus ⅛ tsp; baking soda, ⅛ tsp; buttermilk, ½ cup; egg, 1; sharp Cheddar, 1 cup diced or shredded; basil, 2 tbsp minced plus leaves; grape or cherry tomatoes, 10–12 oz halved.
instructions: Sauté half the onion, bell pepper, and corn in 1 tbsp oil until softened; season and cool. Mix cornmeal, flour, sugar, ⅛ tsp cayenne, baking soda, and salt. Beat buttermilk and egg; combine with dry ingredients and fold in vegetables, cheese, and minced basil.

Sauté remaining onion, add tomatoes, season, and cook until softening. Stir in remaining cayenne and keep warm. Fry batter in ¼-cup portions in a thin film of oil until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Serve topped with tomatoes and basil leaves.
notes: Makes about 8 fritters, or 2 servings. Can be prepared a day ahead; vinegar mixed into milk substitutes for buttermilk.

title: chopped salad with lemon-chipotle dressing
ingredients: Roast chicken, 1 (2 lb); Dijon mustard, 2 tbsp; lemon juice, 2 tbsp; olive oil, 6 tbsp; basil, ⅓ cup minced; shallot, 1 minced; chipotle in adobo, 1–1½ tsp minced; salt and pepper; Persian or Asian cucumbers, 2; heirloom tomatoes, 2; red bell pepper, 1; romaine hearts, 1–2; avocado, 1.
instructions: Pull chicken meat from bones, discard skin, cut into bite-size pieces, and place in salad bowl. Whisk mustard and lemon juice, then olive oil; stir in basil, shallot, and chipotle. Season and mix ¼ cup dressing into chicken.
Add cucumbers, tomatoes, and bell pepper; toss in lettuce and enough dressing to coat. Adjust seasoning, gently fold in avocado, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Use rotisserie chicken; chickpeas may replace chicken for a meatless version.

title: grilled steak with sweet peppers
ingredients: Low-sodium soy sauce, ¼ cup; olive oil, ¼ cup plus 1 tbsp; honey, 2 tbsp; shallots, 2 minced; rosemary, 2½ tbsp minced; salt and pepper; flank or top sirloin steak, 1¼ lb; red and yellow bell peppers, 1 each; poblano, 1; red onion, 1; red pepper flakes, ½ tsp; sherry or balsamic vinegar, 2 tbsp.
instructions: Mix soy, ¼ cup oil, honey, shallots, 1½ tbsp rosemary, salt, and pepper. Coat steak in marinade while preparing peppers. Sauté peppers, poblano, and onion in remaining oil until tender, about 8 minutes; add remaining rosemary and pepper flakes, then vinegar and cook until absorbed.
Grill steak over high heat about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare; rest 5 minutes. Warm pepper mixture, divide among plates, slice steak thinly, and arrange over peppers.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Pepper mixture can be made a day ahead; leftovers make sandwiches or salad.

title: black bean tacos with avocado salsa
ingredients: White onion, 1 chopped; plum tomatoes, 2 diced; serrano chile, 1 minced; cilantro, ¼ cup; lime juice, 3 tbsp plus wedges; avocado, 1 diced; salt and pepper; olive oil, 2 tbsp; red bell pepper, 1 diced; corn kernels from 1 ear; corn tortillas, 8–12; fennel or anise seeds, ¼ tsp; black beans, 2 cans, drained with liquid reserved; crumbled feta.
instructions: Mix ¼ cup onion with tomatoes, chile, cilantro, and lime juice; gently fold in avocado and season. Sauté bell pepper in 1 tbsp oil until softening; add corn and cook 2 minutes. Toast tortillas and keep warm.

Sauté remaining onion with fennel seeds in remaining oil. Add beans by spoonfuls, mashing each addition; thin with reserved liquid to a coarse purée and season. Set out beans, vegetables, salsa, feta, tortillas, and lime for diners to assemble tacos.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Beans and vegetables can be made a day ahead.

title: Lamb kebabs with pomegranate glaze
ingredients: Pomegranate molasses, ¼ cup; shallot, 1 minced; olive oil, 3 tbsp; cumin seeds, 2 tsp crushed; boneless leg of lamb, 1¼ lb cubed; zucchini, 2; red bell pepper, 1; red onion, 1; salt and pepper; mint leaves, slivered.
instructions: Soak 12 bamboo skewers 30 minutes. Mix pomegranate molasses, shallot, 1 tbsp oil, and 1 tsp cumin; coat lamb. Toss zucchini, pepper, and onion with remaining oil and cumin; season.

Prepare grill for high direct heat. Thread lamb on 4 skewers and vegetables on 8; reserve lamb marinade and brush it over vegetables. Season lamb and grill covered, about 5 minutes per side for medium-rare lamb and 6 minutes per side for vegetables. Sprinkle with mint and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Chicken thighs may replace lamb; marinade can be made a day ahead.

title: grilled chicken and corn with smoked paprika rub
ingredients: Smoked paprika, 1 tbsp; ground cumin, 1 tbsp; olive oil, 3 tbsp; lime juice, 3 tbsp; chicken breast cutlets, 1¼–1½ lb; corn, 4 ears; salt and pepper; lime zest, 1½ tbsp; fresh thyme, 1½ tbsp minced.
instructions: Mix paprika and cumin; whisk in oil and lime juice. Put chicken and corn on a baking sheet, brush with mixture, and season. Grill corn over high heat, covered, turning often, until browned and nearly tender, about 10 minutes.
Add chicken and grill until cooked through, about 2½ minutes per side. Transfer to platter, sprinkle with lime zest and thyme, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Chicken can be sautéed indoors; leftover chicken and corn suit sandwiches or salad.

title: roasted mahi mahi with citrus vinaigrette
ingredients: Lemon, 1; olive oil for brushing; mahi mahi fillets, 4; lemon zest, 4 tsp; lime zest, 4 tsp; salt and pepper; Dijon mustard, 2 tsp; extra-virgin olive oil, ⅓ cup; shallot, 1 minced.
instructions: Squeeze 2 tbsp juice from half the lemon and reserve the other half. Heat oven to 400°F. Oil baking sheet; brush fish with oil, rub in lemon and lime zests, squeeze remaining lemon half over fish, season, and roast about 10 minutes.
Whisk mustard with 2 tbsp lemon juice, gradually whisk in olive oil, and stir in shallot; season. Serve fish with vinaigrette.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Dressing can be prepared a day ahead and also suits tuna or halibut.

title: pasta with grilled vegetables and herbs
ingredients: Zucchini, 2; red and yellow bell peppers, 1 each; red onion, 1; olive oil; salt and pepper; penne, ½ lb; extra-virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp; mixed fresh herbs, ½ cup minced; small red chile, 1 minced; kalamata olives, ¼ cup chopped; walnuts, ¼ cup chopped; feta, ½ cup chopped, or Romano.
instructions: Grill oiled, seasoned vegetables over high direct heat, covered, until tender and lightly browned, about 5 minutes per side. Cut into 1-inch pieces. Cook pasta in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta into warmed bowl. Toss with vegetables, extra-virgin oil, herbs, chile, olives, and walnuts; season. Add feta and toss, or pass Romano for diners to grate.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers are good at room temperature or reheated; use any one or two herbs.

title: grilled shrimp and summer squash
ingredients: Dijon mustard, 2 tsp; lemon zest, 1 lemon; lemon juice, 2 tbsp; extra-virgin olive oil, ⅓ cup plus more; serrano chile, 1 minced; marjoram, 1 tsp; basil, 1 tbsp; salt and pepper; colossal shrimp, 1¼ lb; summer squash, 8.
instructions: Soak bamboo skewers 30 minutes and heat grill to medium-high. Whisk mustard, lemon zest and juice, then olive oil; stir in chile and herbs and season. Skewer shrimp using two parallel skewers per group to prevent spinning. Brush shrimp and squash with oil and season.

Grill squash about 5 minutes per side until tender; transfer. Grill shrimp about 4 minutes per side until cooked. Remove shrimp from skewers, cut squash crosswise, toss together with lemon-herb sauce, season, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Dressing can be made a day ahead; peppers, scallops, or chicken can substitute.

title: spaghetti and mussels with tomatoes and basil
ingredients: Spaghetti, 6 oz; olive oil, 2 tbsp; shallot, 1 minced; red pepper flakes, ⅛–¼ tsp; mussels, 1 lb; dry white wine, ⅓ cup; lemon zest, 1 tsp; cherry tomatoes, ¾ lb halved; basil, ½ cup slivered; extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tbsp; salt and pepper.
instructions: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Meanwhile, sauté shallot and pepper flakes in oil until nearly tender. Add mussels, wine, and zest; cover and cook until shells begin to open, about 4 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook until softening, about 2 minutes; discard unopened mussels.
Drain pasta into warmed bowl. Pour mussels and sauce over it; add basil and extra-virgin oil, toss, season, and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Mussel mixture can also be served with crusty bread instead of pasta.

title: turkey cutlets with fresh corn and tomatoes
ingredients: Turkey breast cutlets, 1–1¼ lb; sweet paprika, 1¾ tsp; ground cumin, 1 tsp; salt and pepper; olive oil, 2 tbsp; red onion, ¼ chopped; red pepper flakes, ¼–½ tsp; kernels from 3 ears corn; grape or cherry tomatoes, 10–12 oz; low-sodium chicken broth, ½ cup; marjoram, 2 tbsp minced.
instructions: Season turkey with 1 tsp paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Sauté in 1 tbsp oil, in batches, until browned and cooked, about 3 minutes per side; keep warm.

Sauté onion and pepper flakes in remaining oil. Add corn, season, and cook about 3 minutes; add tomatoes and cook until juicy. Stir in remaining paprika, broth, and turkey juices; boil until syrupy, about 1 minute. Add marjoram, adjust seasoning, and spoon over turkey.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers can be combined with rice or pasta.

title: spicy asian-style baby back ribs
ingredients: Fresh ginger, ⅓ cup minced; shallots, 2 minced; serrano chiles, 2 minced; sugar, ¼ cup; low-sodium soy sauce, ¼ cup; lime juice, ¼ cup; baby back pork ribs, 1¾–2 lb, cut into 2-rib sections; salt and pepper; herb salad mix, 3 cups.
instructions: Mix ginger, shallots, chiles, sugar, soy, and lime juice. Season ribs; rub 2 tbsp mixture over each side and marinate while preparing grill. Stir ¼ cup water into remaining mixture for sauce.

Grill ribs over medium direct heat, meat-side up, 8 minutes; turn and cook 8 minutes. Cover and grill until cooked through, about 8 minutes more per side. Cut into individual ribs, serve on herb salad, and spoon reserved sauce over.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Leftover sauce suits shrimp, fish, or chicken.

title: shrimp salad with potatoes and green beans
ingredients: Lemon wedge and lemon juice, 2 tbsp; green onions, 4, trimmings reserved; dill, 3 tbsp, stems reserved; boiling potatoes, ¾ lb; green beans, ¾ lb; whole-grain Dijon mustard, 1 tsp; extra-virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp; salt and pepper; large shrimp, ¾ lb peeled and deveined.
instructions: Simmer lemon wedge, green onion trimmings, and dill stems in water. Steam potatoes until tender, about 15 minutes; toss with 1 tbsp lemon juice. Steam beans until crisp-tender, about 6 minutes, and add to potatoes. Whisk mustard with remaining lemon juice and oil; mix into vegetables with chopped green onions and dill.
Bring seasoned water to boil, add salt and shrimp, and simmer until just cooked, about 2 minutes. Drain, cut shrimp into pieces, and toss with salad. Season and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Doubles and can be made a day ahead; purchased cooked shrimp speeds preparation.

title: pasta with seared steak, corn, and zucchini
ingredients: Top sirloin or rib eye, 1–1¼ lb; smoked hot paprika, 2¼ tsp; cumin, 2¼ tsp; salt and pepper; spaghetti, 10–12 oz; olive oil, 2½ tbsp; shallots, 3 minced; corn kernels from 3 ears; zucchini, 2 diced; low-sodium beef broth, 1 cup; butter, 1½–2 tbsp; marjoram, ¼ cup minced plus leaves.
instructions: Rub steak with 1¼ tsp each paprika and cumin; season. Cook pasta until al dente. Sear steak in 1 tbsp oil, 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare; rest.

Sauté shallots in remaining oil. Add corn, zucchini, remaining paprika and cumin, season, and cook about 3 minutes. Add broth and reduce until syrupy; stir in butter and marjoram. Toss drained pasta with corn mixture. Slice steak thinly across grain, serve over pasta, and garnish with marjoram leaves.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Sauce can be made while pasta cooks; slice sirloin thinly.

title: tangy summer vegetable salad with bulgur
ingredients: Dijon mustard, 1½ tbsp; sherry vinegar, 3 tbsp; shallot, 1 minced; extra-virgin olive oil, ½ cup; parsley, 3 tbsp minced plus leaves; salt and pepper; chickpeas, 1 can; bulgur, 1 cup; red bell peppers, 2; yellow bell peppers, 2; Asian eggplants, 3; zucchini, 3; blue cheese, ½ cup; walnuts for garnish.
instructions: Prepare grill. Whisk mustard, vinegar, shallot, and oil; stir in minced parsley and season. Toss chickpeas with half the vinaigrette. Simmer bulgur with 1½ cups water until tender, 12–15 minutes; stand covered 5 minutes.

Brush vegetables with oil, season, and grill until browned, about 7 minutes per side. Cut up and toss with chickpeas and enough vinaigrette. Fluff bulgur and place in shallow bowl; top with vegetables, cheese, walnuts, and parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Bulgur and dressing can be made a day ahead; broiling can replace grilling.

title: spice-rubbed grilled chicken
ingredients: Boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1¼–1½ lb; olive oil, 1 tbsp; lemon juice, 1 tbsp; salt and pepper; cumin, 1½ tsp; coriander, ¾ tsp; cinnamon, ¾ tsp; cayenne, ⅛–¼ tsp; lemon zest, 1½ tsp; cilantro, minced.
instructions: Trim chicken, brush with oil and lemon juice, and season. Mix cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and cayenne; sprinkle over both sides of chicken with lemon zest.
Grill over high direct heat, covered, about 6 minutes per side until cooked. Transfer to platter, sprinkle with cilantro, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers can be mixed into couscous salad.

title: Beef skewers with fresh lime-herb sauce
ingredients: Lime juice, ¼ cup plus wedges; vegetable oil, 3 tbsp; low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp; ginger, ¼-inch piece minced; shallot, 1 minced; serrano chile, 1 minced; sugar, 1 tsp; skirt steak, 8–10 oz; cilantro, 2 tbsp minced; mint, 1 tbsp minced; salt and pepper; rice; optional green onions.
instructions: Soak 8 bamboo skewers 30 minutes. Mix lime juice, 2 tbsp oil, soy, ginger, shallot, chile, sugar, and 2 tbsp water. Cut steak into short segments and then lengthwise. Toss with 2 tbsp lime mixture and remaining oil; marinate 10–15 minutes. Add cilantro and mint to remaining sauce.
Thread steak onto skewers, season, and grill over high heat about 3 minutes per side for rare. Serve with rice, sauce, optional green onions, and lime wedges.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Marinade and dipping sauce can be made ahead.

title: buffalo burgers with tomato majoram topping
ingredients: Olive oil, 4 tsp; onion, 1 chopped; serrano chiles, 3 seeded and minced; ground bison, turkey, or beef, 1¼ lb; marjoram, ¼ cup minced; cherry tomatoes, ¾ lb quartered (or 2 large); lime juice; salt and pepper.
instructions: Heat grill. Sauté three-quarters of onion and 2 chiles in oil until tender, about 5 minutes. Mix into meat with half the marjoram; form 4 patties.

Mix tomatoes with remaining onion, chile, and marjoram; season with lime juice, salt, and pepper. Season burgers and grill to desired doneness, about 3 minutes per side for rare. Serve topped with tomato mixture.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Bison is best cooked rare; ground beef or turkey may substitute.

title: asian-style tofu, rice, and broccoli salad
ingredients: Salt; brown basmati or jasmine rice, 1⅓ cups; fresh ginger, ¼ cup sliced; lime juice, ¼ cup; soy sauce or fish sauce, 2 tbsp; chile sauce, 1 tbsp; sesame oil, 2 tsp; firm tofu, 14–16 oz cubed; baby broccoli, broccoli rabe, or broccoli, 1½ lb; cilantro, mint, and basil, ½ cup each minced; roasted peanuts for garnish.
instructions: Cook rice in 2 cups salted water, covered, about 30 minutes; rest 5 minutes, fluff, and cool. Process ginger, lime juice, soy or fish sauce, 2 tbsp water, chile sauce, and sesame oil. Mix sauce with tofu and marinate.
Cut and steam broccoli until tender-crisp, 3–6 minutes; cool and drain. Cut into bite-size pieces and mix with rice, tofu mixture, and herbs. Garnish with peanuts and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Rice and tofu can be prepared the night before; leftover chicken or shrimp can replace tofu.

title: grilled lamb chops with fresh peach salsa
ingredients: Lamb shoulder round-bone chops, 2; cumin, ½ tsp; cinnamon, ¼ tsp; salt and pepper; olive oil; peaches, 2 chopped; red onion, 3 tbsp minced; cilantro, 3 tbsp chopped; chipotle in adobo, ½–1½ tsp minced; lime juice, 1 tsp.
instructions: Rub chops with cumin and cinnamon; season and brush with oil. Mix peaches, onion, cilantro, chipotle, and lime juice; season.
Grill chops over high heat, covered, about 3½ minutes per side for medium-rare. Drain salsa and spoon over chops; serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Salsa also works with other meats or fish.

title: turkey sandwiches with ginger-avocado relish
ingredients: Green onions, 4 minced; olive oil, 2 tbsp; rice vinegar, 5 tsp; ginger, 3½ tsp minced; wasabi paste, 2 tsp; avocado, 1 diced; salt and pepper; turkey breast cutlets, 1¼–1½ lb; sesame oil; country bread, 4 thick slices; butter lettuce, 4 leaves.
instructions: Mix green onions, olive oil, vinegar, 2 tsp ginger, and wasabi; gently fold in avocado and season. Heat grill. Brush turkey with sesame oil, season, and sprinkle remaining ginger on one side. Brush one side of bread with sesame oil.
Grill turkey until cooked, 2–3 minutes per side. Grill bread oiled-side down until golden. Place lettuce and sliced turkey on bread; spoon relish over and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Chicken or fish can substitute; pan-sauté turkey if not grilling.

title: grilled chicken and vegetables with indian spices
ingredients: Plain yogurt, ¾ cup; cilantro, 3 tbsp minced; green onions, 3 minced; salt and pepper; Madras curry powder, 2 tsp; chili powder, 2 tsp; cumin, ½ tsp; coriander, ½ tsp; boneless skinless chicken breasts, 4; Asian eggplants, 4; zucchini, 4; olive oil for brushing.
instructions: Mix yogurt with cilantro and green onions; season sauce. Heat grill. Combine spices. Flatten chicken breasts slightly. Arrange chicken, eggplant, and zucchini on baking sheets; brush with oil, season, and apply spice mixture to both sides.
Grill chicken and eggplant about 5 minutes per side, zucchini about 6 minutes per side, until cooked. Serve with yogurt sauce.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Turkey or fish may replace chicken; bell peppers or potatoes may replace vegetables.

title: Pappardelle with quick bolognese sauce
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; ground beef, 1 lb; pancetta, 2 oz chopped; salt and pepper; dry white wine, ½ cup; whole tomatoes, 1 can (14.5 oz); low-sodium chicken broth, ¾ cup; heavy cream, 1–2 tbsp; nutmeg, ⅛ tsp; egg pappardelle or fettuccine, 12 oz; thyme, 1 tbsp minced; Parmesan.
instructions: Sauté onion in oil until tender and beginning to brown. Add beef and pancetta, season, and cook until beef is no longer pink. Add wine and reduce almost completely. Add tomatoes with juice, broth, cream, and nutmeg; simmer, breaking tomatoes up, until thickened, about 30 minutes.
Cook pasta until tender, drain, and return to pot. Toss with sauce and serve in warmed bowls with thyme and Parmesan.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Sauce can be made ahead or frozen; spaghetti also works.

title: autumn vegetable soup
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; red bell pepper, 1 chopped; rosemary, 1 tbsp minced; red pepper flakes, ¼ tsp; hard-shelled squash, 2 lb cubed; salt and pepper; low-sodium chicken broth, 4 cups plus more; cannellini beans, 1 can; Swiss chard, 1 bunch chopped.
instructions: Sauté onion, bell pepper, rosemary, and pepper flakes in oil until tender, about 12 minutes. Add squash, season, and cook 2 minutes. Add broth and beans; bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer until squash is tender, about 25 minutes.
Add chard and simmer until wilted, about 3 minutes. Thin with broth if desired, adjust seasoning, and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings. Variations may include sausage, other vegetables, beans, pasta, meat, or chicken.

title: spice-crusted tuna with fresh pear chutney
ingredients: Albacore tuna steaks, 4, about 6 oz each; coriander seeds, 2 tsp; cumin seeds, 2 tsp; lemon zest, 2 tsp; salt and pepper; Bosc pears, 2 diced; lime juice, 2 tbsp; cilantro, 2 tbsp minced; ginger, 1 tbsp minced; serrano chile, ½ tsp minced; olive oil, 1 tsp.
instructions: Coarsely grind coriander and cumin; press onto both sides of tuna with lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Mix pears, lime juice, cilantro, ginger, and chile; season chutney.
Sear tuna in oil over medium-high heat to desired doneness, 2–3 minutes per side. Serve topped with chutney.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Apples can replace pears; leftover fish can be added to tomato sauce for pasta.

title: pasta with ratatouille-style vegetables
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp plus more; onion, 1 chopped; red and yellow bell peppers, 1 each; thyme, 2 tsp minced; red pepper flakes; salt and pepper; Italian tomatoes, 1 can (28 oz); dry white wine, ¾ cup; optional sugar; Asian eggplants, 2; zucchini, 2; basil, ¼ cup chopped; rotini or fusilli, 12 oz; fresh goat cheese.
instructions: Sauté onion, peppers, thyme, and pepper flakes in oil until tender, about 15 minutes. Add tomatoes and wine; simmer 15–20 minutes, breaking tomatoes up. Season and add sugar if needed.

Grill or broil oiled, seasoned eggplant and zucchini until tender, about 5 minutes per side. Cut into bite-size pieces and stir into sauce with basil. Cook pasta until al dente, drain, toss with sauce, and serve with goat cheese.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers reheat well with a little water.

title: steak sandwiches with shallot-Dijon mustard aioli
ingredients: Whole peppercorns, 2 tsp; fresh thyme, 4 tsp plus 1 tbsp minced; salt; top round or flank steak, 1¼ lb; mayonnaise, ⅓ cup; shallot, 1 minced; extra-virgin olive oil, 1½ tbsp; sherry vinegar or lemon juice, 1 tbsp; Dijon mustard, ¾ tsp; pepper; olive oil for brushing; country white bread, 8–12 slices; watercress, 1 bunch.
instructions: Coarsely grind peppercorns and mix with 4 tsp thyme and 2 tsp salt. Press mixture onto steak. Mix mayonnaise, shallot, oil, vinegar or lemon, mustard, remaining thyme, and pepper for aioli.

Sear steak in oiled heavy pan about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare; rest 5 minutes. Broil bread slices with a little aioli on one side until browned. Spread aioli on toast, top with watercress and thinly sliced steak, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Extra sauce works with potato salad, vegetables, or fish.

title: chicken and fall vegetables with moroccan flavors
ingredients: Chicken, 1 (5 lb); salt and pepper; sweet paprika, 2 tbsp plus 1½ tsp; cumin, 1½ tsp; red pepper flakes, ¾ tsp; cinnamon, ¾ tsp; lemon, 1; olive oil, 5 tbsp; small sweet potatoes, 2; cauliflower, 1 lb; red onion, 1.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°F and grease a rimmed baking sheet. Dry chicken, season with salt and pepper, loosen breast skin, and rub salt over bird and cavity. Mix paprika, cumin, pepper flakes, and cinnamon; reserve 2½ tsp. Add lemon zest and 2 tbsp oil to remaining spices to make paste. Rub into cavity, under breast skin, and over chicken; add lemon quarters to cavity. Roast 30 minutes.

Toss sweet potatoes, cauliflower, and onion with remaining oil, reserved spices, salt, and pepper. Remove chicken, spoon off most fat, arrange vegetables around it, and roast until thigh registers 165°F, about 40 minutes. Rest chicken 10 minutes, carve, and serve with vegetables.
notes: Makes 4 servings.

title: roasted mahi mahi with olives, capers, and lemon
ingredients: Extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tbsp plus more; mahi mahi fillets, 2; salt and pepper; kalamata olives, ⅓ cup chopped; shallot, 1 minced; capers, 1½ tbsp; lemon juice, 1½ tbsp; lemon zest, 1 tsp.
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Oil small baking dish. Season fish on both sides, place in dish, and brush with oil. Mix olives, shallot, capers, lemon juice and zest, and 1 tbsp oil; spoon over fish.
Roast about 12 minutes, until cooked through. Serve with topping and pan juices.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Olive topping can be made ahead; recipe doubles or triples.

title: mole-style chili with black beans and andouille
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; chicken or pork andouille, 2 diced; zucchini, 3 cubed; cumin, 1 tsp; ancho chile powder, 1 tsp; salt and pepper; diced tomatoes, 2 cans; chipotles in adobo, 2 tbsp minced plus 1 tbsp sauce; unsweetened chocolate, 1 oz; oregano, 1 tsp; black beans, 2 cans.
instructions: Sauté onion in oil until softening. Add sausage and brown, about 5 minutes. Add zucchini, cumin, chile powder, salt, and pepper; stir 1 minute. Add tomatoes, chipotles and sauce, chocolate, and oregano; bring to a boil and simmer 10 minutes.
Add black beans and simmer until zucchini is tender and flavors blend, about 10 minutes; thin with water if needed. Season and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings. Leave out sausage for meatless chili; flavors improve overnight.

title: Lamb burgers with red onion-cumin sauce
ingredients: Plain whole-milk yogurt, ½ cup; red onion, ¾ cup chopped; cumin, ½ tsp; pinch cayenne; salt and pepper; ground lamb, 1¼ lb; allspice, ¾ tsp; pita rounds or hamburger buns, 4; olive oil; tomato, 1 sliced; baby spinach.
instructions: Mix yogurt with one-third of onion, cumin, and pinch cayenne; season sauce. Combine lamb, allspice, remaining onion, salt, and pepper; form 4 patties.

Sear patties in oiled pan over medium-high heat about 5 minutes per side for medium. If using buns, broil oiled cut sides until browned. Place patties in pita pockets or on bun bottoms; add yogurt sauce, tomato, and spinach, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Patties and sauce can be prepared a day ahead.

title: penne with mushrooms and turkey sausage
ingredients: Dried porcini, ¾ oz; olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; hot Italian turkey sausage, ¾ lb; button mushrooms, 10–12 oz; rosemary, 1 tsp; salt and pepper; dry white wine, ⅓ cup; bay leaf, 1; low-sodium chicken broth, ¾ cup; penne, 12 oz; Parmesan, 1 cup grated; parsley.
instructions: Rinse porcini, soak in ¾ cup hot water 20 minutes, drain and reserve liquid, then chop mushrooms. Sauté onion in oil until softening. Add sausage and brown, breaking it up. Add button mushrooms, rosemary, salt, and pepper; cook until softening. Add porcini, wine, and bay leaf; reduce almost dry. Add broth and porcini liquid; simmer until syrupy, about 10 minutes.
Cook pasta until al dente and drain. Add to sauce and toss; remove from heat, stir in Parmesan, season, garnish with parsley, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Pork sausage may replace turkey; sauce can be made a day ahead.

title: braised chicken with lemon-green onion tahini
ingredients: Tahini, ¼ cup; lemon juice, 2 tbsp plus 1 tsp; green onions, 3 chopped; salt and pepper; boneless skinless chicken breasts, 4; egg, 1; Dijon mustard, 2 tsp; lemon zest, 1 tsp; panko, 1 cup; olive oil, 3 tbsp; baby spinach, 6 oz.
instructions: Mix tahini with 2 tbsp lemon juice and 2 tbsp hot water; thin as needed. Stir in two-thirds of green onions and season. Pound chicken to ⅓–½ inch. Beat egg with remaining green onion, mustard, and zest; coat chicken and season. Coat in panko.

Sauté chicken in 2 tbsp oil until browned and cooked, about 4 minutes per side. Toss spinach with remaining oil, salt, pepper, and remaining lemon juice. Divide spinach among plates, top with sliced chicken and tahini sauce.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Extra tahini sauce is good with vegetables, pita, or fish.

title: Chickpea, cauliflower, and potato curry
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; serrano chiles, 2 chopped; ginger, 6-inch piece minced; cumin seeds, 1 tsp; chickpeas, 2 cans with liquid; diced tomatoes, 1 can; lime juice, 1 tbsp; garam masala, ¾ tsp; turmeric, ¼ tsp; cauliflower, ½ head; Yukon gold potatoes, 2; salt and pepper; cooked rice; cilantro, ⅓ cup minced.
instructions: Sauté onion, chiles, ginger, and cumin in oil until onion is tender, about 6 minutes. Add chickpeas and liquid, tomatoes and juice, lime juice, ½ tsp garam masala, and turmeric; boil, then simmer 5 minutes.
Add cauliflower, potatoes, and 1 cup water. Simmer until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes, adding water if needed. Stir in remaining garam masala, season, and serve over rice with cilantro.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Stew reheats well.

title: turkey cutlets with mushrooms and marsala
ingredients: Turkey breast cutlets, 1¼ lb; salt and pepper; olive oil, 2½ tbsp plus more; flour for dredging; shallot, 1 minced; button or cremini mushrooms, 1 lb sliced; dry Marsala, 1 cup; low-sodium chicken broth, ¾ cup; thyme, 3 tbsp minced; butter, 1–2 tbsp; cooked bulgur, 1¼ cups.
instructions: Season turkey. Sauté half in 1 tbsp oil after dredging in flour, about 2 minutes per side; transfer to platter. Repeat with remaining turkey, adding oil as needed.

Sauté shallot in 1½ tbsp oil. Add mushrooms, season, and cook until juices are absorbed. Add Marsala and broth; boil until reduced and slightly thickened, about 8 minutes. Stir in thyme and butter; return turkey and juices and simmer about 3 minutes. Serve over bulgur with sauce.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Chicken can substitute; sliced mushrooms save preparation time.

title: poached eggs with white bean–tomato ragout
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; pancetta, 3 oz chopped; onion, 1 chopped; rosemary, 4 tsp minced; red pepper flakes, ¼–½ tsp; fire-roasted tomatoes, 2 cans; cannellini beans, 2 cans; salt and pepper; white vinegar, 1–2 tsp; eggs, 4–8; grated sharp Cheddar.
instructions: Sauté pancetta in oil until browning. Add onion, rosemary, and pepper flakes; cook until onion tender. Add tomatoes, beans, and ¾ cup water; simmer until thickened, about 15 minutes. Season.
Bring shallow salted water with vinegar to bare simmer. Slip eggs into water individually and poach 3–5 minutes. Divide bean mixture among bowls, top with one or two eggs, cheese, and pepper.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Omit pancetta for meatless version; ragout also makes a side dish.

title: Seared scallops with greens and orzo
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp; onion, ½ chopped; orzo, 1 cup; low-sodium chicken broth, 3 cups plus 3 tbsp; greens, 1 cup chopped; parsley, 3 tbsp minced; thyme, 3½ tsp minced; lemon zest, 1 tsp; salt and pepper; butter, 2 tbsp; sea scallops, ¾ lb; sherry vinegar, 3 tbsp.
instructions: Sauté onion in 1 tbsp oil until tender. Add orzo and brown lightly; add 3 cups broth and simmer, stirring frequently, until almost tender, about 15 minutes. Add greens and cook until wilted and mixture creamy, about 3 minutes. Stir in parsley, 1½ tsp thyme, zest, seasoning, and 1 tbsp butter; keep warm.

Season scallops with salt, pepper, and 1 tsp thyme; sear in remaining oil about 1½ minutes per side. Remove. Boil vinegar and remaining broth in pan until syrupy; off heat, stir in scallop juices and remaining butter. Serve scallops over orzo with sauce and remaining thyme.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Easily doubled; other cooking greens may be used.

title: braised chicken with peppers, olives, and capers
ingredients: Chicken, 1 (about 3½ lb), cut into 10 pieces; salt and pepper; olive oil, 1 tbsp; rosemary, 2 tbsp minced; red or yellow bell peppers, 2 sliced; onion, 1 sliced; pancetta, 1½ oz chopped; red pepper flakes, ½ tsp; diced tomatoes, 1 can; dry white wine, 1 cup; kalamata olives, ⅓ cup; capers, 2 tbsp rinsed.
instructions: Dry and season chicken. Brown in batches in oil with rosemary, about 5 minutes per side; transfer to plate. Sauté peppers, onion, pancetta, and pepper flakes until softening. Add tomatoes, wine, olives, and capers; boil. Return chicken, cover, and simmer on low until breasts are cooked, about 20 minutes.
Remove breasts; cook dark meat 10 minutes more, then uncover and simmer until tender and sauce thickens, about 15 minutes. Return breasts to sauce to heat through; serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftover chicken can be cut up and mixed into sauce and pasta.

title: pasta with lamb and rosemary
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp; onion, 1 sliced; rosemary, 1 tbsp minced; ground lamb, ½ lb; salt and pepper; dry white wine, ¼ cup; diced tomatoes, 2 cans; zucchini, 2 cubed; rotini or rotelle, 10–12 oz; Romano, ½ cup grated.
instructions: Sauté onion and rosemary in oil until tender. Add lamb, season, and cook until no longer pink, breaking it up. Add wine and reduce; stir in tomatoes and zucchini, then simmer until sauce thickens, about 10 minutes.
Cook pasta until al dente, drain, and toss with sauce and Romano. Adjust seasoning and serve with more cheese.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Basil or feta can replace rosemary or Romano; sauce can be prepared ahead.

title: molasses-glazed roast pork and sweet potatoes
ingredients: Pork tenderloins, 2; salt and pepper; light molasses, ¼ cup; Dijon mustard, ¼ cup; rosemary, 1 tbsp minced; red pepper flakes, 1 tsp; sweet potatoes, 1½ lb sliced; olive oil, 2½ tbsp plus more; shallot, 1 minced; chicken broth, ½ cup.
instructions: Heat oven to 400°F. Season pork. Mix molasses, mustard, rosemary, and half the pepper flakes. Toss sweet potatoes with remaining flakes, 1½ tbsp oil, salt, and pepper; arrange on oiled baking sheet and roast 15 minutes.

Brown pork on all sides in remaining oil, about 6 minutes. Place in center of baking sheet; brush pork and potatoes with glaze. Roast about 15 minutes more, until potatoes are tender and pork registers 145°F. Rest on platter.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp pan fat; sauté shallot and browned bits. Add remaining glaze and broth; simmer until slightly thickened. Slice pork, drizzle with sauce, and serve with potatoes.
notes: Makes 4 servings.

title: spaghetti with asian-flavored clams and zucchini
ingredients: Spaghetti, 7–8 oz; sesame oil, 1 tbsp; vegetable oil, 1 tbsp; ginger, 1 tbsp minced; shallot, 1 minced; zucchini, 2 cubed; salt and pepper; clam juice or chicken broth, ½ cup; rice vinegar, 1 tbsp; Asian chile sauce, 1 tsp; Manila clams, 2 lb; cilantro, ¼ cup minced plus garnish.
instructions: Cook pasta until al dente; drain, toss with sesame oil, and keep warm. Sauté ginger and shallot in vegetable oil until aromatic. Add zucchini, season, and sauté briefly. Add clam juice, vinegar, and chile sauce; bring to boil. Add clams and cilantro, cover, and cook until shells open, about 5 minutes.
Season sauce. Pour clams and sauce over pasta, discard unopened clams, garnish with cilantro, and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Doubled recipe requires a large pot; other vegetables can replace zucchini.

title: Lentil stew with smoked turkey and sweet potatoes
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; celery ribs, 3 chopped; thyme, 3 tsp minced; low-sodium chicken broth, 8 cups; smoked turkey leg, 1 lb, meat diced; brown lentils, 1½ cups; sweet potatoes, 1¼ lb cubed; kale or chard, ½ bunch chopped; salt and pepper.
instructions: Sauté onion and celery in oil until nearly tender, about 5 minutes. Add 2 tsp thyme and cook until onion browns. Add broth, turkey, and lentils; bring to boil, then simmer until lentils nearly tender, about 30 minutes.
Add sweet potatoes and simmer about 12 minutes until nearly tender. Add kale and simmer until wilted, about 3 minutes. Season, stir in remaining thyme, and serve.
notes: Makes 6 servings. Reheats well; smoked sausage or vegetable broth and no turkey can be used.

title: sausage and pepper ragout with polenta
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp; Italian turkey or pork sausages, 1 lb; red onion, 1 sliced; red bell peppers, 2 sliced; poblano, 1 sliced; red pepper flakes, ½ tsp; Italian tomatoes, 1 can (28 oz); dry white wine, 1 cup; small onion, ½ chopped; salt and pepper; polenta, 1 cup; Romano, ¾ cup grated; marjoram, 4 tbsp chopped.
instructions: Brown pierced sausages in 1 tbsp oil, about 8 minutes; transfer and pour off all but 2 tbsp fat. Sauté red onion, peppers, chile, and flakes until browning. Add tomatoes and wine; simmer 5 minutes, breaking tomatoes up. Return sausages, cover, and simmer until cooked through, about 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, sauté chopped onion in remaining oil. Add 4 cups water, salt, and pepper; bring to boil. Gradually whisk in polenta and simmer, stirring, until thick, about 18 minutes. Stir in cheese and 1 tbsp marjoram. Add remaining marjoram to ragout, season, and serve over polenta.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers can be layered with sliced sausages and baked with cheese.

title: Fettuccine with wild mushrooms
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; pancetta, 1½ oz chopped; shallots, 3 sliced; thyme or rosemary, 2 tsp minced; wild mushrooms, ½–¾ lb sliced; salt and pepper; low-sodium chicken broth, ¾ cup; egg fettuccine, 6 oz dried or 9 oz fresh; Parmesan, ½ cup grated; parsley.
instructions: Sauté pancetta in oil until brown. Add shallots and thyme; sauté until shallots begin to brown. Add mushrooms, season, and cook until tender. Add broth and simmer until syrupy, about 3 minutes.
Cook pasta until tender, drain, and toss with mushroom mixture over medium heat. Mix in Parmesan, season, divide into bowls, garnish with parsley, and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Use egg fettuccine; affordable shiitake or cremini work well.

title: Halibut with tomatoes, olives, and marjoram
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tsp; onion, ½ chopped; shallot, 1 minced; dry white wine, ⅔ cup; Italian tomatoes, 1 can; red pepper flakes; salt and pepper; halibut, ¾ lb in pieces; kalamata olives, ¼ cup; fresh marjoram, 1–2 tbsp; cooked polenta or rice.
instructions: Sauté onion and shallot in oil until tender, about 5 minutes. Add wine and reduce by half. Add tomatoes and pepper flakes, season, and simmer until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes, breaking tomatoes up.
Season fish and add to sauce; cover and simmer about 4 minutes. Turn fish, add olives and marjoram, and cook until fish is done, about 1 minute. Serve over polenta or rice.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Rice or grilled bread can replace polenta; mahi mahi can replace halibut.

title: Fall vegetable risotto with blue cheese
ingredients: Low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 5 cups; Brussels sprouts, 10 oz quartered; olive oil, 2 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; shiitake mushrooms, ¼ lb sliced; salt and pepper; Arborio rice, 1½ cups; dry white wine, ½ cup; Gorgonzola or blue cheese, ½ cup crumbled; toasted walnuts, ½ cup.
instructions: Bring broth to boil, cook Brussels sprouts until bright and nearly tender, about 4 minutes; remove and keep broth warm. Sauté onion in oil until golden. Add mushrooms, season, and cook until beginning to soften. Add rice and stir until opaque; add wine and stir until absorbed.
Add broth about ¾ cup at a time, stirring frequently until absorbed, until rice is creamy and just tender, about 20 minutes. Mix in sprouts, blue cheese, and pepper; season. Serve with walnuts.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Use vegetable broth for vegetarian version; pancetta may be added.

title: pizza with red peppers, sausage, and feta
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp plus more; small onion, 1 chopped; red bell pepper, 1 sliced; chicken or pork andouille, 2 diced; Italian tomatoes, 1 can; salt and pepper; pizza dough, 1 lb; cornmeal; feta, ¾ cup crumbled; basil, 2 tbsp chopped; marjoram, 1 tbsp chopped.
instructions: Sauté onion and pepper in oil until softening. Add sausage and brown, spoon off excess fat. Add tomatoes and simmer, breaking them up, until sauce is very thick, about 10 minutes; season and cool.

Heat oven to 450°F. Roll dough into 11–12-inch round on cornmeal-dusted pan. Brush with oil and pepper; spread sauce, leaving border, and top with feta. Bake until crust edges brown, about 20 minutes. Rest 5 minutes; sprinkle with herbs and cut into wedges.
notes: Makes 1 pizza; serves 4. Fresh purchased dough and imported San Marzano tomatoes are suggested.

title: roasted salmon with avocado and grapefruit salsa
ingredients: Wild salmon fillet, ¾ lb; olive oil; salt and pepper; ancho chile powder; grapefruit, 1; avocado, 1 cubed; jalapeño, ½ minced; red onion, 3 tbsp minced; cilantro, 2 tbsp minced; lime juice, 1 tbsp.
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F. Place fish in small pan, brush with oil, season with salt, pepper, and ancho chile powder. Roast until almost opaque in center, about 18 minutes.

Cut grapefruit segments free of membranes over a bowl and squeeze juice from membranes. Chop segments and return to bowl. Gently mix in avocado, jalapeño, onion, cilantro, and lime juice; season. Divide fish between plates and top with salsa.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Easily doubled or tripled.

title: braised chicken with onions, rosemary, and sage
ingredients: Chicken breast halves and thighs, 3½ lb; salt and pepper; olive oil, 3 tbsp; onions, 2, one chopped and one in pieces; pancetta, 2 oz chopped; rosemary, 2 tsp minced; sage, 1½ tsp minced; bay leaves, 3; cloves, 4; tomato paste, 1½ tbsp; dry white wine, 1 cup; low-sodium chicken broth, 2 cups.
instructions: Dry and season chicken. Brown in 2 tbsp oil in a deep heavy pan; transfer to plate. Pour off fat, add remaining oil, onions, pancetta, herbs, bay leaves, and cloves. Sauté until onions brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in tomato paste, add wine, and bring to boil, scraping pan.

Return chicken and juices; add broth and simmer over medium-low until breasts cook through, about 20 minutes, turning and basting. Remove breasts; cook thighs about 15 minutes longer until tender. Return breasts to heat through, adjust seasoning, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Season chicken 30 minutes ahead for fuller flavor.

title: stir-fried tofu with mushrooms and greens
ingredients: Low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, 1 cup; soy sauce, 2 tbsp; cornstarch, 1 tbsp; red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp; sesame oil, 1 tbsp; pepper, ¾ tsp; Asian chile sauce, ½ tsp; sugar, ½ tsp; vegetable oil, 1 tbsp; green onions, ¼ cup minced; ginger, 2 tbsp minced; shiitake mushrooms, ¼ lb sliced; broccoli rabe, 1 bunch; firm tofu, 1 lb cubed; salt.
instructions: Whisk broth, soy, cornstarch, vinegar, sesame oil, pepper, chile sauce, and sugar. Heat vegetable oil in wok or large pan; stir-fry green onions and ginger until aromatic. Add mushrooms and stir 30 seconds; add broccoli rabe and stir 1 minute.

Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until greens are crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. Add tofu gently. Re-stir broth mixture and add; cook until sauce thickens and tofu is hot, 2–3 minutes. Season and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Serve with rice; Chinese broccoli can replace broccoli rabe.

title: broccoli rabe, feta, and mint pasta
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; optional pancetta, 2 oz chopped; onion, 1 chopped; red pepper flakes; Italian tomatoes, 1 can (28 oz); salt and pepper; broccoli rabe, 2 bunches; rotini, 14½–16 oz; mint, ¼ cup chopped; feta, ¾ cup crumbled.
instructions: Sauté optional pancetta in oil until brown. Add onion and pepper flakes and cook until tender, about 8 minutes. Add tomatoes and 1 cup water; boil, breaking tomatoes up, then simmer until thickened, 15–20 minutes. Season.

Boil broccoli rabe in salted water until crisp-tender, about 4 minutes; remove. Cook pasta in same water until al dente, return rabe to pot briefly to heat. Drain; toss with sauce and mint, stir in half the feta, season, and top with remaining feta.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Goat cheese or pecorino can replace feta; other short pasta shapes work.

title: spiced roasted halibut with fennel and onion
ingredients: Cumin, 1½ tsp; chili powder, 1½ tsp; cinnamon, 1 tsp; turmeric, ¼ tsp; fennel bulb, 1 in wedges; red onion, 1 in wedges; olive oil, 3 tbsp; salt and pepper; halibut fillets, 2; cilantro.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°F. Mix spices. Toss fennel and onion with 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp spice mixture, salt, and pepper; spread in pan and roast until tender and browned, turning once, about 35 minutes.
Oil fish pan; brush fish with oil, season both sides with remaining spice mixture, salt, and pepper. Roast until almost firm, 5–8 minutes. Serve fish with vegetables and cilantro.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Avoid overcooking halibut.

title: Chicken with mustard and walnut coating
ingredients: Boneless skinless chicken breasts, 4; egg, 1; Dijon mustard, 2 tbsp; panko, ½ cup; walnuts, ¼ cup chopped; shallot, 1 minced; lemon zest, 1½ tsp; dry mustard, ½ tsp; cayenne, ⅛ tsp; olive oil, 2 tbsp; salt and pepper.
instructions: Heat oven to 400°F. Pound chicken to ⅓–½ inch. Beat egg with Dijon. Mix panko, walnuts, shallot, lemon zest, dry mustard, and cayenne. Heat oil in ovenproof pan. Coat chicken with egg mixture, season, then coat with panko mixture.
Brown chicken in pan about 2 minutes on first side; turn and transfer pan to oven. Bake about 8 minutes, until springy and cooked through. Serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Prepare vegetables while chicken bakes.

title: smoky black bean soup
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; red bell peppers, 4 diced; celery ribs, 3 diced; onion, 1 chopped; smoked turkey, chicken, or pork sausage, 1–2 chopped; cumin, 1 tsp; smoked hot paprika, 1 tsp; low-sodium chicken broth, 4 cups; black beans, 2 cans; diced tomatoes with juice, 1 can; water or broth, 2 cups or as needed; salt and pepper.
instructions: Sauté peppers, celery, and onion in oil until onion tender, 5–6 minutes. Add sausage and brown, about 2 minutes. Add cumin and paprika and stir 1 minute. Add broth, beans, and tomatoes; bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer at least 20 minutes and up to 45 minutes, thinning as needed.
Season with salt and pepper, ladle into bowls, and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings. Improves with longer simmering or reheating; can vary beans, sausage, or vegetables.

title: pork chops with horseradish applesauce
ingredients: Center-cut loin pork chops, 2; salt and pepper; rosemary, 2 tsp minced; sage, 2 tsp minced; unsweetened applesauce, 1 cup; cream-style horseradish, 2 tsp; sugar, 4 tsp; olive oil, 1 tbsp; shallot, 1 minced; dry vermouth or white wine, ½ cup; low-sodium chicken broth, ½ cup.
instructions: Season chops with salt, pepper, and 1½ tsp each rosemary and sage. Mix applesauce, horseradish, and sugar. Brown chops in oil over high heat, 1–2 minutes per side; lower heat, cover, and cook to 145°F, about 3–4 minutes per side. Transfer and tent.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat. Sauté shallot briefly; add vermouth, broth, and remaining herbs. Boil until syrupy, about 2 minutes. Return chops and turn to coat. Serve with sauce and applesauce.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Use thermometer and avoid overcooking.

title: tuna with shallot gremolata
ingredients: Albacore tuna steak, 1½ lb; mustard seeds, 1 tsp; fennel seeds, 1 tsp; salt and pepper; lemon, 1; flat-leaf parsley, ⅓ cup chopped; shallot, 1 minced; olive oil, 1 tsp.
instructions: Cut tuna into 4 pieces. Press mustard and fennel seeds onto both sides; season. Finely grate lemon zest into bowl; mix with parsley and shallot for gremolata.
Sear tuna in oil over medium-high heat to desired doneness, 2–3 minutes per side. Serve with gremolata.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Gremolata is also good with chicken, fish, or stew.

title: Chicken with squash, turnips, and shiitakes
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp; boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1¼ lb; salt and pepper; onion, 1 chopped; sage, 1 tbsp minced; butternut squash, 1 lb cubed; small turnips, 2 bunches, cubed, greens reserved; chicken broth, 1½ cups plus 1 tbsp; shiitake mushrooms, ½ lb; flour, 1¼ tsp.
instructions: Brown seasoned chicken in 1 tbsp oil, about 1½ minutes per side; transfer. Sauté onion and sage until tender. Add squash, turnips, and 1½ cups broth; bring to boil, cover, and simmer until chicken tender, about 25 minutes.

Sauté mushrooms in remaining oil until tender. Chop greens from one bunch turnips. Add mushrooms and greens to chicken, cover, and cook until greens wilt, about 5 minutes. Mix flour with remaining broth, stir into pan, and simmer until sauce thickens, about 2 minutes. Adjust seasoning and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Cubed prepared squash may be used; turnip greens are optional.

title: sausage and mushroom risotto
ingredients: Low-sodium chicken broth, 5 cups; olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; Italian sausage, ¾ lb; button mushrooms, 10–12 oz sliced; Arborio rice, 1½ cups; dry vermouth or white wine, ½ cup; salt and pepper; Parmesan or Romano, ½ cup grated; parsley or basil.
instructions: Bring broth to boil, then keep warm over low heat. Sauté onion in oil until nearly tender, about 5 minutes. Add sausage and cook until no longer pink, breaking it up. Add mushrooms and sauté until beginning to soften. Stir in rice until opaque; add vermouth and stir until absorbed.
Add broth about ¾ cup at a time, stirring frequently until absorbed and rice is creamy and just tender, about 20 minutes. Stir in cheese, season, and serve with herbs.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Leftovers can become risotto cakes with egg yolk and panko.

title: Cauliflower and tofu curry
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; firm tofu, 14–16 oz cubed; hot curry or vindaloo paste, 1 heaping tbsp; diced tomatoes, 1 can; cauliflower, 1 head in florets; cooked brown basmati or jasmine rice.
instructions: Sauté onion in oil until nearly tender, about 5 minutes. Add tofu and warm through. Add curry paste and stir to coat. Add tomatoes and juice, cauliflower, and 1½ cups water. Bring to boil, cover, and simmer over medium-low until cauliflower is tender and sauce thickens, about 20 minutes, adding water if needed.
Serve over warmed rice.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Reheats well; prepared curry paste is a convenient flavoring.

title: chicken and noodles with sweet root vegetables
ingredients: Large chicken thighs, 4; salt and pepper; flour for dredging; extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp; red onion, 1 chopped; parsnips, ½ lb; carrots, ½ lb; sage or rosemary, 1 tbsp minced; dry white wine, ½ cup; low-sodium chicken broth, 1¼ cups; wide egg noodles, 6 oz; optional parsley.
instructions: Season chicken, dredge in flour, and brown in 1 tbsp oil about 4 minutes per side; transfer. Sauté onion, parsnips, carrots, and sage until onion tender, about 10 minutes. Add wine and reduce by half, scraping browned bits.

Return chicken, add broth, bring to boil, cover, and simmer, turning once, until tender, about 20 minutes. Uncover and reduce liquid slightly. Cook noodles in salted water until tender, drain, toss with remaining oil, and serve topped with chicken and vegetables; garnish with parsley.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Chicken thighs reheat well; leftovers can be saved for another meal.

title: turkey burgers with radicchio slaw
ingredients: Mayonnaise, 3 tbsp; whole-grain Dijon, 1½ tbsp; capers, 3 tbsp minced; ground turkey, 1¼ lb; thyme, 1 tbsp minced; extra-virgin olive oil, 4 tbsp plus more; shallot, 1 minced; salt and pepper; hamburger buns, 4; radicchio, 1 head sliced; balsamic vinegar, 1½ tbsp.
instructions: Mix mayonnaise, mustard, and 1½ tbsp capers for sauce. Mix turkey, thyme, remaining capers, sautéed shallot, salt, and pepper; form 4 patties. Brush bun cut sides with oil and pepper.

Cook patties in oiled pan about 5 minutes per side, until done. Toss radicchio with remaining oil, salt, pepper, and vinegar. Broil buns cut-side up until golden. Assemble buns with patties, sauce, and slaw; serve with remaining slaw.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Patties and sauce can be made a day ahead; ground chicken also works.

title: pizza with onions, mushrooms, and brie
ingredients: Olive oil, 3 tbsp plus more; onions, 2 sliced; rosemary, 1 tbsp minced; salt and pepper; dry white wine, ¼ cup; mushrooms, ½ lb sliced; shallot, 1 minced; parsley, 1 tbsp minced plus garnish; cornmeal; pizza dough, 1 lb; Brie, ½ lb, rind removed and cut up.
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Sauté onions and rosemary in 1½ tbsp oil with salt and pepper until golden, about 20 minutes. Add wine and reduce; transfer onions. Sauté mushrooms and shallot in remaining oil until tender and juices evaporate; stir in parsley.

Oil and cornmeal a baking sheet. Roll dough into 10–11-inch round and transfer. Brush with oil; spread onions and mushrooms over dough, leaving border; top with Brie. Bake 12–15 minutes until crust brown and cheese melted. Cut into wedges and garnish with parsley.
notes: Makes 1 pizza; serves 4. Any mushrooms work; sausage or pancetta can be added.

title: broiled leg of lamb with orange and fennel
ingredients: Shallot, 2 tbsp minced; thyme, 2 tbsp minced; orange zest, 2 tbsp; fennel seeds, 2¼ tsp crushed; boneless leg of lamb, 1¼–1½ lb; salt and pepper; olive oil, 1 tbsp plus more; fennel bulb, 1 in wedges; red onion, 1 in wedges; dry vermouth, ⅓ cup; low-sodium chicken broth, ⅓ cup.
instructions: Mix shallot, thyme, orange zest, and fennel seeds. Season lamb and rub each side with 1 tbsp herb mixture; brush with oil. Toss fennel and onion with oil, remaining herb mixture, salt, and pepper; arrange on oiled baking sheet. Reserve 1 tbsp herb mixture for sauce.

Position lamb 4 inches from heat and broil to 125–130°F, about 8 minutes per side; rest under foil. Move vegetables closer to heat and broil 3–4 minutes per side. Degrease broiler pan, set on stovetop, deglaze with vermouth, reduce syrupy, then add broth and reduce. Stir in reserved herbs and lamb juices; season and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Seasoning mixture can be prepared a day ahead.

title: chicken sauté with thyme, lemon, and chile
ingredients: Olive oil, 2 tbsp; chicken breast cutlets, ¾ lb; salt and pepper; shallot, 1 minced; thyme, 2 tsp minced; serrano chile, ½–1 minced; dry white wine, ⅓ cup; lemon juice, 2 tbsp.
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Season chicken and sauté until cooked through, 2–3 minutes per side; transfer to warmed plates. Add remaining oil, shallot, thyme, and chile; sauté until shallot softens. Add wine and lemon juice; boil, scraping browned bits, until syrupy, about 1 minute.
Stir in chicken juices, adjust seasoning, spoon sauce over chicken, and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings. Easily doubled; leftovers reheat well over rice or noodles.

title: curried mahi mahi with chinese broccoli
ingredients: Onion, ⅓ cup chopped; shallots, 3 halved; cilantro stems, 2 tbsp; lemongrass, 2 tbsp chopped; ginger, 2 tbsp chopped; turmeric, 1 tbsp; cumin, 1 tbsp; red pepper flakes, ¾ tsp; vegetable oil, 1 tbsp; mahi mahi, 1½ lb in pieces; plain yogurt, 1½ cups; clam juice, 1½ cups; optional coconut milk or cream, 2 tbsp; Chinese broccoli or broccoli rabe, 2 bunches; cilantro leaves.
instructions: Process onion, shallots, cilantro stems, lemongrass, ginger, turmeric, cumin, and pepper flakes to a fine paste. Heat oil in pan; stir-fry paste 1 minute. Add fish and cook, turning, 2 minutes. Whisk yogurt smooth and add with clam juice and optional coconut milk; simmer, turning fish, until nearly cooked, about 6 minutes. Transfer fish to plate.
Simmer broccoli in sauce until wilted and sauce slightly thickens, about 4 minutes. Return fish to heat through, garnish with cilantro, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Sauce also suits scallops or chicken; lemon zest may replace lemongrass.

title: sautéed pork with parsnips
ingredients: Extra-virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp; parsnips, 10 oz cubed; shallots, 2 minced; thyme, 2 tsp plus ½ tbsp minced; salt and pepper; wide egg noodles, 3 oz; pork tenderloin, 8–10 oz sliced; flour for dredging; low-sodium chicken broth, 1 cup; dry vermouth, ½ cup.
