instructions: Sauté parsnips in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes. Add shallots and 2 tsp thyme; season and cook until browning, about 4 minutes. Transfer. Cook noodles in salted water until tender, drain, and toss with 1 tbsp oil and 1½ tbsp thyme; keep warm.

Season pork, dredge in flour, and brown in remaining oil about 2½ minutes per side; transfer. Add broth, vermouth, and parsnips to pan; boil, scraping browned bits, then simmer until parsnips tender, about 8 minutes. Return pork and juices; cook until done and sauce thickens, about 2 minutes. Finish with thyme and serve with noodles.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. Carrots, onions, rutabaga, or sweet potatoes can replace parsnips.

title: Chipotle-spiced Buffalo chili
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 chopped; red bell peppers, 2 cubed; ground bison or beef, 1 lb; salt and pepper; ground dried chipotle, 2 tsp; cumin, 1 tsp; cinnamon, ¼ tsp; cloves, ⅛ tsp; diced tomatoes, 2 cans; pinto or kidney beans, 2 cans; oregano, 1 tsp; optional plain yogurt, 1 cup; optional lime zest, 2 tsp.
instructions: Sauté onion and peppers in oil until onion is tender, about 10 minutes. Add meat, season, and cook until no longer red, breaking it up. Add chipotle, cumin, cinnamon, and cloves; stir until fragrant. Add tomatoes, beans, oregano, and 1 cup water; cover and bring to boil. Simmer over medium-low about 30 minutes.
Mix optional yogurt and lime zest. Adjust chili seasoning, serve in bowls, and top with lime yogurt if desired.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings. Beef or turkey can replace bison; chili improves with reheating.

title: pasta with fennel, tomatoes, olives, and shrimp
ingredients: Olive oil, 1½ tbsp; fennel seeds, ½ tsp; fennel bulb, 1 sliced, fronds reserved; onion, 1 sliced; red pepper flakes; salt and pepper; Italian tomatoes, 1 can; kalamata olives, ¼ cup; dry white wine, 3 tbsp; shrimp, ½ lb; spaghetti, 7–8 oz.
instructions: Bring salted pasta water to boil. Heat oil in pan, toast fennel seeds 10 seconds, then add fennel, onion, and pepper flakes; season and sauté until tender and browned at edges, about 10 minutes. Add tomatoes, olives, and wine; simmer, breaking tomatoes up, until thick, about 5 minutes. Add shrimp and cook until opaque, about 5 minutes.
Cook pasta until al dente while shrimp cooks. Drain and toss with shrimp sauce; adjust seasoning, garnish with fennel fronds, and serve.
notes: Makes 2 servings; can be doubled. American shrimp are noted as a sustainable choice.

title: white bean stew with porcini and winter squash
ingredients: Dried porcini, 2–2½ oz; olive oil, 1 tbsp; onions, 2 chopped; serrano chiles, 2 minced; sage, 2 tsp minced; butternut squash, 2 lb cubed; salt and pepper; cannellini beans, 2 cans with liquid; low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, 2 cups; parsley.
instructions: Rinse porcini and soak in 3 cups very hot water about 20 minutes. Sauté onions, chiles, and sage in oil until tender, about 8 minutes. Add squash, season, and sauté about 5 minutes; add beans with liquid and broth.
Drain porcini through sieve, reserving soaking liquid; add liquid and chopped mushrooms to pot. Simmer until squash is tender and flavors blend, about 20 minutes. Season, serve in bowls with parsley.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings. Sausage, pancetta, smoked turkey, or rosemary may be added or substituted.

title: roasted black cod with Korean flavors
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp plus more; shallot, 1 minced; ginger, 2 tsp minced; serrano chile, 1½ tsp minced; low-sodium soy sauce, ⅓ cup; brown sugar, ¼ cup; rice vinegar, 3 tbsp; water, 3 tbsp; sesame oil, 1 tbsp; black cod fillets, 4; green onions, 2 sliced.
instructions: Heat oven to 400°F. Sauté shallot, ginger, and chile in olive oil until tender, about 3 minutes. Add soy, sugar, vinegar, and water; simmer until reduced to ¾ cup, about 6 minutes. Remove from heat, stir in sesame oil, and reserve a little sauce for brushing.
Oil baking pan, add fish skin-side down, brush with reserved sauce, and roast about 10 minutes until cooked. Serve sprinkled with green onions and pass remaining sauce.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Extra sauce keeps refrigerated and works with chicken, shrimp, rice, or vegetables.

title: Cauliflower, onion, and greens risotto
ingredients: Low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 4 cups; olive oil, 1 tbsp; onion, 1 coarsely chopped; cauliflower, ½ head in florets; Arborio rice, 1½ cups; dry white wine, ½ cup; beet greens or other greens, 1 bunch sliced; Parmesan, 1 cup grated; marjoram, 1½ tbsp minced; salt and pepper.
instructions: Bring broth and 1 cup water to boil; keep hot. Sauté onion in oil until golden, about 8 minutes. Add cauliflower and heat through; stir in rice until opaque. Add wine and stir until absorbed. Add hot broth about ¾ cup at a time, stirring frequently and allowing absorption, until rice is nearly tender, about 15 minutes.

Add greens and continue stirring, adding liquid about ½ cup at a time, until greens wilt and rice is creamy and just tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in Parmesan and marjoram, season generously, and serve.
notes: Makes 4 servings. Any cooking greens may be used.

title: tri-tip roast with brussels sprouts and shallots
ingredients: Tri-tip beef roast, 1¾–2 lb; salt and pepper; sweet paprika, 2¼ tsp; caraway seeds, 2 tsp; dried marjoram, 2 tsp; dry mustard, 1 tsp; cayenne, ½ tsp; olive oil, 3½ tbsp plus more; Brussels sprouts, 1 lb halved; small shallots, ¾ lb halved plus 1 large minced; low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp plus 2 tsp; dry vermouth, ½ cup; beef or chicken broth, ½ cup; butter, 2 tsp.
instructions: Heat oven to 450°F with racks centered and lower. Season beef; place on rack in shallow roasting pan. Mix 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp caraway, ½ tsp marjoram, mustard, cayenne, and 1 tbsp oil; rub over beef. Toss Brussels sprouts and halved shallots with remaining 2½ tbsp oil, 1 tbsp soy, remaining caraway, and 1 tsp marjoram; roast on lower rack. Roast beef to 120°F for rare, about 20 minutes, or desired doneness. Rest 15 minutes; roast vegetables until tender and browned, about 25 minutes.

Use 1 tbsp beef-pan fat to sauté minced shallot. Deglaze roasting pan with vermouth, scraping browned bits, and pour into saucepan; reduce to syrupy. Add broth, remaining paprika and soy; reduce syrupy. Off heat, add beef juices, butter, and remaining marjoram; season. Slice beef and serve with vegetables and sauce.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.

title: pizza dough
ingredients: Active dry yeast, 1 tbsp; warm water (110°F), ¾ cup plus 2 tbsp; extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tbsp; all-purpose flour, 2¾ cups; salt, 1 tsp.
instructions: Sprinkle yeast over warm water and stand until foamy, about 5 minutes. Add oil, ½ cup flour, and salt to mixer bowl; mix. Add remaining flour gradually and knead with dough hook until smooth and not sticky, about 10 minutes.

Form dough into ball, place in oiled bowl, turn to coat, cover, and rise in warm place until doubled, 1–2 hours. Turn onto floured surface and press, stretch, or roll to desired shape, usually about 12 inches wide and ¼ inch thick.
notes: Makes 1 lb dough.

title: saffron rice
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; small shallot, 1 chopped; basmati rice, 1 cup; salt; saffron threads, ¼ tsp crumbled.
instructions: Sauté shallot in oil until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add rice, 2 cups water, ½ tsp salt, and saffron; bring to boil. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer about 20 minutes. Fluff with fork and serve.
notes: Makes 4–5 servings.

title: brown aromatic rice
ingredients: Brown basmati or jasmine rice, 1⅓ cups.
instructions: Bring 2 cups salted water to boil. Add rice and return to boil. Cover, reduce heat to low, and cook 30 minutes. Turn off heat and stand covered 5 minutes; fluff and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.

title: basic cooked quinoa
ingredients: Quinoa, 1 cup; salt and pepper; olive oil, 2 tsp.
instructions: Rinse quinoa well. Bring 2 cups water to boil; add quinoa and ½ tsp salt. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer until water is absorbed and quinoa tender, about 20 minutes. Drizzle with oil, season, toss with fork, and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.

title: basic cooked bulgur
ingredients: Quick-cooking bulgur wheat, 1 cup; salt.
instructions: Combine bulgur with 1½ cups cold water and a little salt. Bring to boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer until just tender, 12–15 minutes. Turn off heat and stand covered at least 5 minutes. Fluff and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.

title: basic cooked couscous
ingredients: Broth or water, 1 cup; olive oil, 1 tsp; salt and pepper; quick-cooking couscous, 1 cup.
instructions: Bring broth to boil; add oil and ½ tsp salt. Stir in couscous, remove from heat, cover, and stand 5 minutes. Fluff, season, and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.

title: herbed polenta
ingredients: Olive oil, 1 tbsp; small onion, ½ chopped; salt and pepper; polenta, 1 cup; fresh marjoram or thyme, 1 tbsp chopped; Parmesan or Romano, ¾ cup coarsely grated.
instructions: Sauté onion in oil until tender, about 5 minutes. Add 4 cups water, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper; bring to boil. Gradually whisk in polenta. Return to boil, reduce heat, and simmer, stirring frequently, until thick, about 18 minutes. Stir in cheese and marjoram; serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.

title: olive oil-mashed potatoes
ingredients: Yukon gold potatoes, 2 lb peeled; salt and pepper; milk, 1 cup; extra-virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp.
instructions: Cover potatoes with water by 1 inch; add 1 tsp salt and bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer until tender, 25–30 minutes. Warm milk until bubbles form around edges; remove from heat and stir in olive oil.
Drain potatoes and return to pot. Mash until smooth, gently mix in milk-oil mixture, season, and serve.
notes: Makes 4–6 servings.
